OpenAI is positioning Astra for assignments such as changing a complex codebase, building a working web application, or producing a document that follows a company’s templates. Sol is the cheaper option for routine coding, writing, and workflows that require several steps.

results.content:
TL;DR

 OpenAI has launched GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, promising improved performance and greater efficiency across professional and everyday tasks.
 Early testers reported problems with unproductive loops, premature task completion, and confusing responses despite impressive benchmark results.
 OpenAI believes some reviewers missed last-minute model improvements and acknowledges that there’s still room to improve the user experience. [...] OpenAI

But impressive benchmark scores don’t necessarily make for an impressive coworker. Among those given early access, a recurring frustration was the models’ tendency to get caught up in unproductive loops, abandon assignments prematurely, and produce summaries that were unnecessarily difficult to understand. In one particularly frustrating instance, days of attempted coding improvements reportedly left a project performing worse than before. [...] However, the models behind some of those reviews may not be quite the same ones you’re getting today. OpenAI’s Thibault Sottiaux explained on X that the company made substantial changes in the final three to four days before launch, which he believes some reviewers missed. Still, he acknowledged that improvements in creative taste and ease of use remain on the company’s agenda.

results.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, and early testers push back
results.content:
Browne tested Astra before launch and posted a letter he says he sent to OpenAI. He praised it as a code reviewer and for 3D, games and computer use. OpenAI fixed a few of his complaints, he wrote, but not enough for him to recommend it.

> “I do not like 6.2 Astra. I would not choose this over Opus 5.5 for my work as a developer,” Browne wrote. [...] Testers who had the model before launch were less sure. Research group Epoch AI found Astra trailed Anthropic’s Claude Fable 5.2 on realistic work tasks. Developer Theo Browne said he would not pick it over Anthropic’s Opus 5.5.

## Cheaper per token and per task

In the API, Astra costs $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens. That is 20% less than GPT-6 Astra. Cached input is 60% cheaper, at $0.40. Sol keeps GPT-6.1 Sol’s prices of $2 for input and $10 for output. [...] OpenAI has released GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol, and cut the price of its top model by 20%. Astra is its frontier model for the hardest projects, according to the company’s announcement. Sol is the cheaper model for everyday work. Both went live on Tuesday in ChatGPT Work, Codex and the API.

> “We believe GPT-6.2 Astra is the best model in the world for scientists,” OpenAI wrote.

GPT-6.2 Astra—a frontier model built for your hardest projects. It sets new highs on evals across professional work and scientific research at less than a third of the cost per task of GPT‑6 Astra.

results.title: OpenAI model release dates: o3, GPT-5.5 and GPT-6 Astra, Sol and Luna in order · Think Facility
results.content:
GPT-6 kept two of those names and moved one of them. Astra is the new top, and the models page now says to use it if you're "not sure where to start". GPT-6 Sol is the middle model, there to "balance intelligence and cost", which is the job Terra had. Luna is still the cheap one. There's no GPT-6 Terra on the page at all. [...] ## Astra, Sol, Terra, Luna: which GPT is which

This is the part that confused me. In July, OpenAI stopped using plain version numbers and gave the GPT-5.6 family three names: Sol "for frontier capability", Terra "for a balance of intelligence and cost" and Luna "for efficient, high-volume workloads". Sol was the top. [...] That makes "Sol" ambiguous. GPT-5.6 Sol is last generation's flagship and GPT-6 Sol is this generation's mid-tier. They're separate models with separate IDs (`gpt-5.6-sol` and `gpt-6-sol`), so check which one a benchmark or a forum post means before you compare anything.

| Model | Role | In / out per 1M |

| GPT-6 Astra | Flagship | $10 / $50 |
| GPT-6 Sol | Middle | $2 / $10 |
| GPT-6 Luna | Cheap, high volume | $0.10 / $0.50 |
| GPT-5.6 Sol | Last generation's top | $4 / $20 |

results.title: GPT-6.2 | ChatGPT Learn
results.content:
# GPT-6.2

GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol launch in ChatGPT Work, Codex, and the API. Choose Astra for your hardest projects or Sol for everyday coding and writing.

## What’s new

### ChatGPT Work

Use Astra or Sol in Work on the web, desktop, or mobile with Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, or Edu. Enterprise and Edu admins must first enable the models in workspace settings. [...] ### Responses API

Use `gpt-6.2-astra` or `gpt-6.2-sol` in the Responses API. Both models support Ultrafast at launch.

In standard, single-agent mode, you can change reasoning effort or switch from plain text to structured output between replies. Append a `configuration_update` item before the next user message and keep the request-level settings unchanged. Keeping earlier input intact helps preserve reasoning across turns and keeps that input eligible for prompt caching. [...] On supported consumer plans, new Work chats default to Sol at Light reasoning effort. Enterprise workspaces with model access default to Sol at Medium. If you see the Power slider, open Advanced to choose a model and reasoning effort.

### Codex

In the Codex app and CLI, choose Astra to trace a bug across services, fix it, and test the affected workflows. Choose Sol to review a pull request or revise code in response to feedback. Use the model picker in the app or `/model` in the CLI.
